subject: Higher-Order CR with compRelSEM in semTools

messages.author: 14ce58f9c4879902
messages.subject: Higher-Order CR with compRelSEM in semTools
parts:
Hi,
McDonald (1999) defined two reliability measures for higher-order factors: omega-total (𝜔T) and omega-hierarchical (𝜔h). From my understanding both are interesting when evaulating the reliability of a higher-order model (e.g., Cheung et al., 2023).

The compRelSEM package of the semTools package outputs a general statistic when a higher factor is defined. Does this general statistic refer to the 𝜔T or 𝜔h?
Wouldn't it be useful to have an option to see them both?

Best,
Lucas

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Higher-Order CR with compRelSEM in semTools
parts:
Omega hierarchical vs. total is distinguished for bifactor models, sometimes confusingly referred to as having a hierarchical structure (which I believe is with respect to the clustering of items within group/method factors).  You are talking about a higher-order factor, in which case the only "true" variance of interest is the variance of the higher-order factor.  Flora has a recent tutorial discussing this distinction, although the software is already out of date.  If only authors would contact software developers about their writing about the developer's work, their own work would be so improved...

https://doi.org/10.1177/2515245920951747

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
